heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, video generation, and multimodal creative production.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected premium hero built as a full-width editorial overlay: a bright Techjockey-orange base with a subtle mesh gradient, white typography, and layered abstract AI forms behind the copy. Keep the hero text-led but not centered-only: align the headline slightly left within a wide composition, then place a horizontal proof strip beneath the CTAs. Since the page must feel senior-designed and not generic, make the hero feel like a launch poster rather than a product screenshot. Use the first media moment later in the page as an immersive split story for Seedream and Seedance, with alternating light and dark sections; reserve a dark section for Seedance to satisfy contrast requirements. CTA buttons should be accent orange with strong contrast, and decorative CSS elements should include soft orbs, faint grid lines, and gradient meshes for depth.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a bold orange editorial hero to match the ad message, then switch immediately to a compact logo trust band so the page does not feel like a generic SaaS intro.
Use a visual-first how-it-works section next, but not as a grid; make it a 3-step horizontal narrative with one strong illustration or model flow panel.
Alternate background treatments across adjacent sections: orange hero, white trust band, soft-grey process, white proof, pale-neutral feature spotlight, then a more contained pricing/CTA block.
Separate Seedream and Seedance into distinct product stories with different compositions: one spotlight-plus-grid, one split-panel list, so the page rhythm changes between image and video.
Keep testimonials as a compact carousel/static spotlight instead of another dense grid, so proof feels curated rather than repetitive.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore the 3-step workflow, trusted logos, key features, pricing, and get started with AI visual generation.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand-orange with layered abstract editorial shapes and subtle floating prompt chips
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Use the provided headline and subheadline, keep the copy content-first, and make the CTA a large solid button labeled exactly 'Get started'. Add a short 3-bullet value list beneath the CTA for continuity with the ad message. This is the loudest section and should feel premium, immediate, and creative-professional.

Place trust immediately after the hero because the traffic is warm and the proof type is logos. Use 3-6 recognizable client/brand logos in a clean flex-wrap row; if usable logos are unavailable, replace with a restrained metric strip. Keep it visually quiet but prominent, with no motion or marquee.

Show a 3-step process: prompt or upload, generate with Seedream/Seedance, refine and export. Keep it under 60 seconds in message and rhythm. Use a visual-first split panel rather than a card grid, with one side illustrating the flow and the other side containing the three steps. This section should feel fast, simple, and confidence-building.

Build credibility with industry-specific proof using the available testimonials, but keep the emphasis on outcome language: creative speed, synchronized audio-video, multimodal editing precision. Use a spotlight testimonial at the top and supporting proof tiles beneath it. Since logos are already used in the trust bar, this section should deepen confidence through expert validation rather than repeat the same proof pattern.

Because there are two productSections and each has 5+ features, use tabs with a preview panel instead of a flat static grid. Let Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro occupy two distinct tabs or toggles, each opening a focused preview state. Seedream should highlight image fidelity, typography, composition, and editing. Seedance should highlight text-to-video, synchronized audio, lip-sync, and cinematic control. Keep the two product stories visually different so the page does not feel repetitive.

Use a compact comparison-style pricing block with two cards, but visually privilege the video generation offer only if it aligns with the click intent; otherwise keep both equal. The CTA on every price card must still read exactly 'Get started' if shown as a button, even though the source text says Get Quote. Keep the cards clean and editorial, not salesy.

With 5 testimonials available, use a compact carousel or spotlight slider rather than a dense grid. Prioritize quotes from creative directors, video producers, and art directors. Keep the section short and curated, using one highlighted quote with supporting cards or slides. This should feel like expert endorsement, not a review dump.

End with a focused conversion block that re-centers the value proposition and makes the next step obvious. The form should be a single premium card with minimal fields, strong spacing, and a full-width mobile CTA labeled exactly 'Get started'. Do not add secondary CTA text. This is the strongest conversion moment after proof and product detail.

Optional footer-adjacent utility area only; keep it minimal and standard. If used, show a simple static horizontal logo or partner strip without marquee motion. If no additional credible logos exist, omit this section entirely and let the footer remain clean.

blueprint.designPersonality: An editorial, high-clarity AI landing page with Techjockey’s orange-led identity, premium whitespace, and strong trust-first structure. It should feel like a sophisticated launch page for creative professionals: confident, organized, and visually intelligent rather than flashy or generic.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use abstract AI-generated visual compositions, layered product mock shells, and polished model cards rather than literal dashboards. The hero can feature floating prompt chips, sample output thumbnails, and elegant media strips. Trust should be built primarily with a prominent logo band, enterprise-ready badge row, and concise proof metrics.
blueprint.additionalInstructions:
PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo placement above a bold headline, concise supporting copy, and a short bullet-value list; primary conversion focus is immediate and above the fold.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form landing page with a strong hero, followed by a dedicated lead-capture form block and stacked product feature sections; emphasis on sequential scanning rather than dense multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content blocks with minimal visual ornamentation, primarily utility-first and form-led rather than decorative; no evidence of glassmorphism or elaborate hover treatment.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA in the hero and additional section-level CTA placement for product inquiry/demo intent; conversion language is direct and action-oriented, with limited CTA variety.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module present in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference HTML; likely minimal or standard utility footer if present elsewhere.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible structure; logo mark in hero and icon bullets/ticks are the primary visual assets, with no embedded product imagery, galleries, or media panels in the provided snippet.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked product-specific sections with a label, headline, descriptive paragraph, CTA, and feature list; content is progressive-disclosure oriented and optimized for skimmable benefits.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form card inserted directly after hero, using hidden tracking inputs and a compact visible field set; form behaves as a conversion anchor rather than a secondary contact element.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, conversion-focused presentation with no explicit motion system visible in the HTML snippet.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is intended to generate qualified leads for two advanced generative AI products aimed at professional buyers. The audience is solution-aware and evaluating capabilities, so the structure should quickly explain what each model does, why it matters, and how to inquire. Because the strongest trust signal is logos, credibility should be led by logo-first proof and reinforced through testimonial support from relevant creative roles. The page should feel efficient and premium rather than playful, with a split hero that prioritizes message clarity and conversion. Since the content is long, the layout must stay balanced and highly scannable, with strong CTAs, an early form block, pricing/quote support, and a sticky top strip to maintain conversion access throughout the scroll.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
